duration.text: The Applied chemistry at Shanghai Normal University is a 4 Years long program for international students, taught in English.

fees.text: Application Fee: $ 150 USD Service Fee: $ 50 USD Tuition fee: $ 2888 USD/per year ￥ 20800 CNY/per year

materials.text: 1. Passport scan copy (the information page of the passport, it is recommended to be in JPG or PNG format, or in PDF format); 2. Applicants who have already studied or worked in China are required to submit a scanned copy of their visa or residence permit in China at the same time. 3. Recent personal ID photo (2-inch ID photo in electronic format. It is recommended to be in JPG or PNG format); 4. Scanned copies of the complete high school transcript (if you are currently enrolled in university, please also provide the transcript of the courses you have completed at the university); 5. Scanned copy of high school graduation certificate (For fresh graduates, a pre-graduation certificate can be provided first. The expected graduation date should be earlier than August 31, 2025; During the registration process, the original graduation certificate must be verified and a copy must be submitted). 6. Language proficiency proof materials (such as HSK certificates, etc.); 7. Students applying for art-related majors such as music, dance, performance, film and television, and fine arts are required to submit their personal works or performance videos. 8. One to two recommendation letters; 9. The "Foreigner Physical Examination Form" issued by the hospital; 10. Certificate of No Criminal Record (provided by the public security bureau or the school of your education); 11. Asset proof (bank deposit certificate of no less than 5000 US dollars in the name of the applicant or the applicant's parents); 12. For those under the age of 18, a guarantee letter from a guardian is required;

requirements.text: 1. At least 16 years old, with good physical and mental health. 2. Non-Chinese nationality: The determination method is in accordance with the relevant provisions of the "Document No. 12 from the Ministry of Education's Department of Foreign Affairs [2020]". 3. High school graduation 4. Chinese proficiency requirement: A valid HSK certificate must be submitted. 1) Chinese Language and Chinese International Education Major (International students form their own classes): The HSK 4 level should generally be no less than 180 points. 2) For art-related majors: The HSK 4 level must reach 180 points (with each individual score generally not lower than 60 points); 3) Science and Engineering Majors: HSK Level 4 must reach 195 points (with each individual score generally not lower than 65 points); 4) For liberal arts and economics management majors: HSK Level 4 must score 210 points or HSK Level 5 must score 180 points (with individual scores generally not lower than 70 points) Those holding the following certificates may apply for exemption from submitting the HSK certificate. 1) The score of the SAT II Chinese (with Listening) examination is ≥ 600; 2) Have completed the IB Chinese HL course and achieved a score of 6 or above; 3) Have completed A-level Chinese courses and achieved grades of A or above; 4) Through the AP Chinese course or other proof; 5) Education at the secondary school level is conducted in the Chinese language. 6) Obtain the pre-scholarship program completion certificate from the Chinese government.
